_doc: Concurrency declaration for `gz check` steps (GHI #835). MEASURED, never assumed: each step ran alone against a marker file and anything newer afterwards is something that step wrote, which catches writes outside git as well as tracked ones. The GHI is explicit that this declaration is the deliverable and the speedup only its consequence -- 'A parallel runner over steps with an undeclared dependency is a flaky gate, which is strictly worse than a slow one.' A step absent from `steps` fails the gate closed (tests/governance/test_check_step_concurrency.py); a new step is DECLARED, never defaulted. `measured_seconds` is a dated record for routing attention, never a threshold anything enforces. TIMINGS RE-MEASURED 2026-08-28 (GHI #903), each step run alone, all 58 reporting success. `class` was NOT re-derived: it comes from a different protocol (marker file plus newer-than check) and re-deriving it casually would put a guess where a measurement is. One step had drifted past 2x -- 'Handoff documents' read 28.67s and measures 4.05s -- and that is exactly the harm a stale attention-router does: it named the third-most-expensive step in the gate, so an agent profiling `gz check` for cost investigated it before measuring it. 'Test (changed)' is carried forward unmeasured on purpose: it substitutes for 'Test' only in --fast scope and its cost is a function of how dirty the working tree is, not of the step.
protocol: Writers run serially, in list order, before any read-only step starts -- except a reader carrying `overlaps_writers`. Read-only steps then run concurrently. The boundary is a CONSERVATIVE DEFAULT against UNDECLARED dependencies, not the preservation of a named edge. CORRECTED 2026-08-28 (GHI #905): this field read that the phasing 'preserves the one measured producer->consumer edge (Behave builds dist/, Validate default scopes reads it)'. That edge does not exist and never did -- `gz validate --distribution` is the static T0 audit and walks the SOURCE tree, the wheel-reading arm of T0 is tests/test_packaging.py inside the Test step and it builds its own wheel hermetically into a tmpdir, and the audit exits 0 with dist/ moved aside. See the Behave entry for the full evidence. What actually carries safety here is the OPT-IN polarity: a reader waits for the writer lane unless it has been MEASURED not to read writer output and declares `overlaps_writers`, so an unmeasured step is conservative rather than silently racing. The two writers were measured disjoint (Behave -> dist/, Docs build -> site/), so nothing measured forbids overlapping them either; that is an OPEN question worth about 3.9s which needs a WRITER-side safety argument the reader-side flag does not carry, and it is deliberately not taken. AMENDED 2026-08-28 (GHI #904): one reader may overlap the writer lane. Only Test carries overlaps_writers today -- Behave writes exactly one path (dist/py_gzkit-*.whl) and Docs build writes only under site/, while Test writes nothing and every dist//site/ reference under tests/ is an exclusion naming those trees 'not live state'. The flag is OPT-IN: absence means wait. OUTCOME, measured rather than projected: 72.09s -> 60.82s wall (~16%), NOT the ~50% a naive max(33.01, 31.99) predicts. Adding step wall-times treats cores as free, and they are not -- the Test step runs unittest-parallel across every core, so overlapping it with Behave fills idle cores rather than eliminating a serial block. Parallelism efficiency moved 2.61x -> 3.07x (user/wall), which is the honest description of what this bought. _MAX_CONCURRENT_STEPS carries the same warning for the reader pool and it applies here too.

Behave.why: Builds the wheel into dist/ as part of the distribution feature. NOTHING IN THE GATE READS THAT WHEEL -- corrected 2026-08-28 (GHI #905), where this field claimed `gz validate --distribution` consumed it and was the reason a naive parallel runner would be flaky. `gz validate --distribution` is the STATIC T0 audit: `audit_distribution` says so in its own first line ('no wheel build required') and walks pyproject include globs against the SOURCE tree, which is what the T0 contract in docs/governance/trust-doctrine.md asks of it -- 'A T0 audit MUST detect missing package data without depending on downstream installation evidence'. The wheel-reading arm of T0 is tests/test_packaging.py, inside the Test step, and it builds its OWN wheel into a tmpdir 'to keep build hermetic and avoid polluting the repo's dist/'. Verified at bdd5bc4b: the audit exits 0 with dist/ moved aside entirely. Behave is a writer because it WRITES; no step waits on it. SHARDED x4 2026-08-28 (GHI #906). Measured in-gate on a 10-core host: baseline 62.07s mean gate / 47-49s step, sharded x4 50.45s gate / 33.85s step, sharded x8 50.54s mean gate / 22-23s step. FOUR IS THE SATURATION POINT, not the fastest way to run behave alone -- past roughly 34s Behave stops being the critical path and every further shard is contention with Test for no wall-clock return, so x8 halves the step again and moves the gate not at all. Scenario conservation is exact across every arm (408 passed, 0 failed). Safe because features/environment.py gives every scenario a fresh mkdtemp and chdir with no before_all, and because exactly one feature file drives the dist/ write above, so the file partition keeps that write inside a single process; tests/governance/test_behave_sharding.py fails if a second wheel-building feature appears.

Docs build.why: mkdocs renders the whole site/ tree. Nothing else in the step set reads site/, so this writer is isolated -- but it is still a writer and is never run concurrently with anything.

Test.why: Carries `overlaps_writers` (GHI #904): MEASURED not to read anything a writer produces, so it runs while the writer lane is still open instead of idling 31.99s behind 33.01s of writers it has no edge to. Measured 2026-08-28 with the same marker protocol that produced `class`, on BOTH sides: Behave wrote exactly one path (dist/py_gzkit-0.34.5-py3-none-any.whl) and Docs build wrote 515 paths all under site/ -- independently confirming the `paths` those two entries already declare -- while Test is read_only (writes nothing) and every dist/ or site/ reference under tests/ is an EXCLUSION naming those trees not-live-state. Absence of a known conflict was NOT the bar; a two-sided measurement was. The flag is opt-in, so a future step that skips that measurement keeps waiting rather than silently racing.

Test (changed).why: Fast-scope substitute for Test; same read-only shape, not measured by the probe.

Validate default scopes.why: Reclassified from `writes` under GHI #891, and only once the write became IMPOSSIBLE rather than rare. `check_sync_parity` used to establish parity by PERFORMING `sync_all()` and restoring afterwards; it now renders into `surface_write.capture_surface_writes` and byte-compares, so no input -- clean tree or drifted -- reaches a write. That distinction is the whole point: a static `read_only` on a validator that writes only on drift would be a scheduling guarantee that is false exactly when the gate is red, which is when a concurrent step would read a torn mirror. Witnessed by `tests/test_validate_sync_parity.py::SyncParityDriftedTreeIsNonMutatingTest`, on ctime rather than mtime -- the old restore called `os.utime`, so an mtime probe read clean against a tree that had just been rewritten.
